questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of two numbers whose first common multiple is the product of the two numbers?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 3 and 7 because they are co-prime, meaning they have no common factors other than 1, so their least common multiple is their product, 21. 3 and 6 share a common factor of 3, so their least common multiple is 6, not their product. 4 and 6 share a common factor of 2, so their least common multiple is 12, not their product. 3 and 12 share a common factor of 3, so their least common multiple is 12, not their product.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct rule for checking divisibility by 4?
choices: If the last digit is even, the number is divisible by 4
If the number formed by the last two digits is divisible by 4, the number is divisible by 4
If the last two digits are 00, the number is divisible by 4
If the number ends in 4, the number is divisible by 4
questions.solution: The correct answer is that if the number formed by the last two digits is divisible by 4, the number is divisible by 4. This is because 100 is divisible by 4, so the remainder of any number when divided by 4 depends only on its last two digits. The other options either give incorrect rules (like checking only the last digit) or are too limited in scope (like checking only for 00 at the end).

questions.stem: If the product of two numbers is a prime number, what must be true about the numbers?
choices: One number is 1 and the other is prime
One number is 0 and the other is prime
questions.solution: The correct answer is that one number is 1 and the other is prime. A prime number has only two factors: 1 and itself. Therefore, the only way two numbers can multiply to give a prime is if one is 1 and the other is the prime itself. The other options either incorrectly assume both numbers are prime (which is not always true) or include 0, which would make the product 0, not a prime number.

hi.solution: सही उत्तर यह है कि एक संख्या 1 है और दूसरी अभाज्य है। एक अभाज्य संख्या के केवल दो गुणनखंड होते हैं: 1 और स्वयं। इसलिए, दो संख्याओं के गुणनफल के रूप में एक अभाज्य संख्या प्राप्त करने के लिए, आवश्यकता है कि एक संख्या 1 हो और दूसरी संख्या अभाज्य हो। अन्य विकल्प गलत रूप से दोनों संख्याओं के अभाज्य होने का अनुमान लगाते हैं (जो हमेशा सत्य नहीं है) या 0 शामिल करते हैं, जिसके कारण गुणनफल 0 हो जाएगा, जो एक अभाज्य संख्या नहीं है।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses appropriate mathematical terminology.

questions.stem: If a number is divisible by both 2 and 3, it is also divisible by which of the following?
questions.solution: If a number is divisible by both 2 and 3, it is also divisible by 6. This is because 6 is the least common multiple of 2 and 3. 4, 8, and 10 are not guaranteed to divide the number.

hi.stem: यदि कोई संख्या 2 और 3 दोनों द्वारा विभाज्य है, तो यह निम्नलिखित में से किस द्वारा भी विभाज्य होती है?
hi.solution: यदि कोई संख्या 2 और 3 दोनों द्वारा विभाज्य है, तो यह 6 द्वारा भी विभाज्य होती है। इसका कारण यह है कि 6, 2 और 3 का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य है। 4, 8 और 10 संख्या को आवश्यक रूप से विभाजित नहीं करते।

questions.stem: If the product of two numbers is a prime number, which of the following could be the numbers?
questions.solution: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself. For the product of two numbers to be prime, one of the numbers must be 1 and the other must be a prime number. Only the option 1 and 2 satisfies this condition, as 1 × 2 = 2, which is prime. The other options result in products that are not prime numbers.

hi.stem: यदि दो संख्याओं का गुणनफल एक अभाज्य संख्या है, तो निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी संख्याएं हो सकती हैं?
hi.solution: एक अभाज्य संख्या के ठीक दो अलग-अलग धनात्मक भाजक होते हैं: 1 और स्वयं। दो संख्याओं के गुणनफल के अभाज्य होने के लिए, एक संख्या 1 होनी चाहिए और दूसरी संख्या अभाज्य संख्या होनी चाहिए। केवल विकल्प 1 और 2 इस स्थिति को पूरा करता है, क्योंकि 1 × 2 = 2, जो अभाज्य है। अन्य विकल्पों के गुणनफल अभाज्य संख्याएं नहीं होती हैं।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation is accurate, maintains the same meaning, and uses appropriate mathematical terminology as found in Hindi textbooks.
